rules.title: Prohibition Against Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market
rules.requirement: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not price-fix using algorithmic pricing. A residential dwelling unit is any primary residence, excluding medical/long-term care and detention facilities. Price fixing using algorithmic pricing means using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other real estate lessors. The purpose that makes it unlawful is to coordinate, recommend or implement rental prices, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Nonpublic competitor information includes, but is not limited to, prices, supply levels, security deposits, ideal occupancy levels, lease contract termination and renewal dates, or any other material terms. It covers such information that is less than 365 days old and not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. The Division of Housing, or any private citizen alleging to be aggrieved, may bring alleged violations to the Hoboken Municipal Court. On conviction, a violator is subject to one or more of the following: penalties under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, a fine of up to $2,000, or community service of up to 90 days.
rules.key_value: Penalties on conviction, one or more of: N.J.S.A. 40:49-5 penalties; fine up to $2,000; community service up to 90 days. Nonpublic competitor information is data less than 365 days old.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords of any residential dwelling unit (any primary residence) in Hoboken, excluding medical/long-term care and detention facilities. No unit-count, building-age or landlord-size limits.
coverage.other_conditions: Residential dwelling unit is defined as any primary residence, excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities.

rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rules.effective_date_note: Adopted unanimously on July 9, 2025. Section Four provides that the ordinance takes effect immediately upon passage and publication as provided by law. The publication date is not in the captured documents, so no exact effective date is recorded. The law-firm alert (DX06) gives 'effective July 2025', which is consistent with adoption that month. The ordinance is in force on the query date.

effective_date_formula.verbatim: This Ordinance shall take effect immediately upon passage and publication as provided by law.

citation_aliases: Ordinance Amending and Supplementing Chapter 158 (Rent Increases) of the Hoboken City Code by Adding a New Section 158-2
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.conflict_note: New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) was approved July 20, 2026 and takes effect July 1, 2027. Its Section 6(b) prohibits municipalities from enacting ordinances that conflict with the act. Once the act is effective, it may preempt this ordinance to the extent the two conflict. Whether any conflict exists is unresolved.
rules.review_note: The ordinance title and Section One add a new Section 158-2 to Chapter 158, but the section heading in the body reads § 154-8. Section Five authorizes the Clerk and Corporation Counsel to renumber at codification, so § 158-2 is used as the primary citation and § 154-8 is kept as an alias. On June 4, 2025, before first reading, a county-jail penalty of up to 90 days was removed. The adopted text provides community service instead.
rules.source_notes: Primary source is the official Hoboken legislative record of the adopted ordinance (DX01). The Morgan Lewis alert (DX06, August 2026) is a secondary summary that cites 'ch. 158-2' and gives only a month-level effective date, consistent with DX01.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.

known_gaps.reason: DX01 names Chapter 158 (Rent Increases) as the chapter being amended, but the text of Hoboken's rent control provisions was not captured. The Hoboken code-publisher sources (D032–D034) are link-only.
